candidates.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation
candidates.content: LiDAR is a critical sensor for autonomous driving and robotics, yet it remains vulnerable to adverse conditions such as fog, rain, transparent objects, and low-reflectance surfaces. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL) addresses these limitations by capturing the complete return waveform as a histogram, preserving rich reflection characteristics including multi-path echoes and weak signals. While recent Transformer-based approaches have demonstrated promise on FWL data, two fundamental bottlenecks remain: high computational cost from redundant tokens in low-intensity background regions, and limited generalization due to scarce annotated training data. We address both bottlenecks by exploiting the physical structure inherent to FWL data. First, we propose FWL-ToPM, a token pruning and merging mechanism that leverages intensity distributions to selectively reduce tokens while retaining critical waveform content. Second, we introduce FWLAug, a data augmentation framework designed as a regularization method that preserves waveform structure, retaining the Time-of-Flight waveform of each ray and the frustum geometry, to improve generalization to unseen scenes. candidates.title: SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset
candidates.content: The pursuit of fair and equitable AI in human-centric tasks is critically hindered by the inherent biases and privacy risks of real-world datasets, which offer imbalanced representations of identity and often contain sensitive personal information. Consequently, state-of-the-art generative models trained on this skewed data exhibit unfair performance, particularly in identity-preserving generation. In this work we propose a pipeline for controllable generation of dataset with diverse faces for generative models training and finetuning. We achieve this by expanding foundational Arc2Face diffusion model with a flow matching generative model in the manifold of identity embeddings. We demonstrate that such approach achieves both goals of generative fidelity and label diversity not present in real human-centric datasets. As a result we collect and further contextualize a highly balanced identity-centric dataset of humans named SynthFaces. By design, our released images and identities are synthetic, reducing direct reliance on real personal images; we empirically check identity separation with a nearest-neighbor non-leakage metric. candidates.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
candidates.content: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. candidates.title: A Safety and Immunogenicity Trial of OCU500, ChAd36 Vector Encoding SARS-CoV-2 Spike Vaccine Via Intranasal and Inhalational Routes in Previously Vaccinated Adults
candidates.content: [PHASE1] ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) | 适应症: COVID-19. This phase 1 randomized, open-label, dose-escalation clinical trial evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of OCU500, a ChAd36 Vector Encoding SARS-CoV-2 Spike Vaccine, in healthy adults aged 18-64 who previously completed a primary COVID-19 vaccination series and at least one booster. The study evaluates two dose levels (1×10\^10 viral particles (VP) and 5×10\^10 VP) and two routes of administration (intranasal and inhaled). The trial includes 80 participants across four study arms (20 per arm). The primary objective is to evaluate the safety and reactogenicity of a single dose of OCU500 administered in previously vaccinated healthy adults.

candidates.title: Understanding Patent Thickets
candidates.content: Prescription drug manufacturers typically apply to the US Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) for patents to protect their products from generic competition. The primary patent on a drug covers the core active ingredient and generally lasts 20 years. Because these patents are often granted early in drug development, however, the effective period of patent protection after US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval is usually 7 to 12 years. Once that period ends, generic versions may enter the market and compete with the brand-name drug, often leading to a rapid and substantial decline in price. The statutory framework for drug patents is established in the Hatch-Waxman Act of 1984. In addition to patent protection, brand-name drugs may qualify for periods of exclusivity granted by the FDA, which may run concurrently with patents or separately.

candidates.title: Treating In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest With Sodium Bicarbonate—Reply
candidates.content: In Reply In their letter about our recent BIHCA trial, Dr Gelbenegger and colleagues focus on the numerical differences in 30-day survival (12% vs 9.1%) and 30-day favorable neurological outcome (8.1% vs 5.4%) between groups. As noted, the trial was not powered for these outcomes and the results are uncertain. The 95% CIs for the risk ratio for 30-day survival ranged from 0.84 to 1.88 and for 30-day favorable neurological outcome from 0.82 to 2.34. As such, our results were compatible with harm, no effect, and benefit. Until well-conducted and sufficiently powered randomized clinical trials establish a benefit of sodium bicarbonate during cardiac arrest, consistent with international guidelines, we do not believe it should be administered routinely.

candidates.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element
candidates.content: CRISPR tiling mutagenesis of the 10-kb human MYC locus mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. An ultraconserved RNA regulatory element was identified that controls MYC localization and can be therapeutically targeted to suppress cancer cell growth in patient-derived tumor organoids.
